title: Cluster & Pool Inkling Daily Export — 2026-11-27
content:
Sheet export (raw) - informal notes and quick recon.

COLUMNS:	date	cluster	pool	region	avg_gpu_util_pct	median_batch_size	pct_time_above_80	fragmentation_index	idle_sockets	preemptions	run_notes
2026-11-26	cluster-alpha	pool-lowpri	us-west1	42	8	6	0.18	12	3	steady mid-week background; small microbursts 03:00-04:00 PST
2026-11-26	cluster-alpha	pool-prod	us-west1	78	32	47	0.06	2	0	spike during rollout window; ~2s tail latency bump
2026-11-26	cluster-beta	pool-gpu-reservoir	us-east4	65	12	22	0.12	6	1	fragmentation creeping in after reservation spillover
2026-11-26	cluster-gamma	pool-interactive	eu-central	84	24	61	0.04	1	0
2026-11-26	cluster-delta	pool-cache	ap-southeast	35	6	3	0.22	18	5	high idle from scheduled maint earlier in day

Quick metrics (hand calc):
- Fleet average util (weighted by claimed sockets): ~61% today (approx).
- High-risk pools: pool-interactive (eu-central) avg 84% with pct_time_above_80 61% -> <20% headroom left for microbursts.
- Fragmentation index correlates most strongly with idle_sockets across lowpri/cache pools (r~0.7 in quick sample).

Interpretation summary (notes to self / for infra-ops):
- We are seeing the expected regional skew: EU and US prod pools carry the majority of tail risk. APAC has lower utilization but high fragmentation (lots of small idle sockets).
- Recent reservation spill (INF-342) moved 120 sockets into reservoir pools in us-east4; pool-reservoir shows higher median_batch_size and modest util but fragmentation rising -> reservations not packing tightly.
- Canary rollout earlier today contributed to a 2s tail latency bump on cluster-alpha prod; appears bounded and recovered via autoscaling fallback.

Immediate suggested actions (owner suggestions):
- Short term: move 8 lowpri sockets from cluster-delta/ap-southeast to cluster-beta/us-east4 overnight (low impact maintenance window). Owner: Miguel. ETA: 2026-11-28 02:00 UTC.
- Medium term: raise pack threshold for reservations in us-east4 to reduce fragmentation_index by ~0.05. (PR in flight: infra#789). Owner: Priya. ETA: next deploy.
- Monitoring: add alert for pct_time_above_80 > 50% sustained 10m for any pool tagged prod-interactive. Owner: Ben.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- What is the real cost tradeoff of consolidating APAC cache sockets vs. keeping them separate for locality? Quick guesstimate: consolidation could reduce idle socket waste by ~12 sockets but increase p99 by ~100ms for APAC users. Need input from solutions-eng.
- Does reservation policy enforcement respect preferred packing when burst_capacity is enabled? Observed odd packing in cluster-beta -> file a follow-up ticket if confirmed.

Action log / TODOs:
- [x] Pull daily slice and compute fragmentation_index (Sofia)
- [ ] Schedule overnight socket move (Miguel)
- [ ] Validate reservation packing change on staging (Priya)
- [ ] Deploy pct_time_above_80 alert rule (Ben)

Notes on methodology / fields:
- avg_gpu_util_pct: aggregator = mean over 1-minute samples across claimed sockets in pool.
- fragmentation_index: simple metric = idle_sockets / (claimed_sockets + 1) weighted by pool priority. Rough, intended for signal not absolute.
- pct_time_above_80: fraction of 1m samples where util >= 80% over 24h window.

References & quick links:
- Infra dashboard (ops): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ops/gpu-utilization
- Reservation spill incident: https://linear.app/REDWOOD/issue/INF-342
- PR for packing heuristics: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/789

Free-form notes / brainstorm (messy):
- 'Inkling' export: name is intentionally rough — this sheet is a quick recon dump to capture smells not full analysis.
- Thought: experiment with short-lived "packing drains" that move lowpri tasks out for 15m windows during EU tail spikes; could be scripted as a temporary policy in the routing layer. Potential pitfalls: flapping and cache cold-start.
- Keep an eye on cluster-gamma; sustained >80% on interactive pools means we either need more capacity or lower beta rollout concurrency.

End of export.
